Heard Sri Diwakar Tiwari, learned counsel for applicant, Sri Shiv Narayan Pandey, learned counsel for informant and Sri Markandey Singh, learned Brief Holder for State.

Applicant- Kallu Singh, has approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. in Case Crime No.23 of 2023 under Sections 342, 376, 427,
506 I.P.C., Police Station- Pailani, District - Banda after rejection of his Bail Application vide order dated 14.03.2023 passed by Sessions Judge, Banda.

In the present case, an F.I.R. was lodged by victim (a married woman aged about 34 years having three children) that her husband was staying at Mumbai for the purpose of work and on 22.12.2022 at about 10.00 p.m., the present applicant came inside the house of victim, however, when alarm Kallu Singh vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180276019/
1 was raised, he ran away.

sentences.text: Victim further alleged on next day i.e. 23.12.2023 when she was at field applicant and one unknown person forcefully took her on a motorcycle and raped at a scheduled place and she was confined till 15.01.2023, where her signatures were obtained on blank papers and she was put under threat and was repeatedly raped and when returned on 15.01.2022, she lodged an F.I.R. on 21.01.2023.
The same version has been stated in the statement recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. except some exception.

Learned counsel for applicant submits that it was a case of consensual relationship and he refers the documents annexed along with application i.e. a notarized agreement of marriage as well as that a complaint was given by the victim to Superintendent of Police, Banda that she has married with applicant on her own will without any force.

Learned counsel also submits that delay in lodging F.I.R. of five days remained unexplained and that family members of victim has not taken any step despite the victim was missing for almost more than three weeks.
He also points out that alleged unknown person was not identified as well as medical examination has not been supported the prosecution case.
Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is behind the bars since 10.02.2023 and in case, he is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in trial.
Learned A.G.A. for State has opposed the bail and has referred the statement of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. that allegation remained consistent.
Learned counsel for informant also refers that during forceful stay of victim with applicant, he has taken signatures of victim on blank papers.
LAW ON BAIL - A SUMMARY (A) The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail.

(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.

(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is no need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.

However, a Court cannot completely divorce its decision from material aspects of the case such as allegations made against accused; nature and gravity of accusation; having common object or intention; severity of punishment if allegations are proved beyond reasonable doubt and would result in a conviction; reasonable apprehension of witnesses being influenced by accused;
tampering of evidence; character, behaviour, means, position and standing of accused; likelihood of offence being repeated; the frivolity in the case of prosecution; criminal antecedents of accused and a prima facie satisfaction of Court in support of charge against accused.

The Court may also take note of participation or part of an unlawful assembly as well as that circumstantial evidence not being a ground to grant bail, if the evidence/ material collected establishes prima facie a complete chain of events.

Parity may not be an only ground but remains a relevant factor for consideration of Kallu Singh vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180276019/
2 application for bail.

sentences.text: In the present case, age of victim is about 34 years and she is a married woman having three children.
According to her case, applicant has put her in confinement for about more than three weeks, however, neither her husband nor her relatives have lodged a missing report.

So far as, documents are concerned which are in the form of marriage agreement cannot be taken note as since they are not part of case diary, still considering that victim has never raised any alarm during her stay with the applicant as well as she further took five days to lodge an F.I.R. after she returned and delay prima facie has not been explained and since the statement of victim during investigation has already been recorded, therefore, applicant who is in jail since 10.02.2023 has made out a case for bail.

However, in order to remove apprehension, applicant shall not enter within the boundaries of District Banda for a period of four months from today except for the purpose of this case or with prior permission of learned Trial Court.
Meanwhile learned Trial Court shall take all endeavour to record the statement of victim expeditiously, in accordance with law.

Let the applicant- Kallu Singh be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment or exemption from appearance on the date fixed in trial.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iii) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his Kallu Singh vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180276019/

(iv) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months after release of applicant,
if there is no other legal impediment.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
The bail application is allowed.
It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only for the purpose of adjudicating the present bail application.
